svg.aria-label: Current QueryDesk architecture and request flow
svg.text: CURRENT ARCHITECTURE / ENGLISH QUESTION TO GOVERNED DATABASE ANSWER
Includes published domain knowledge and existing guardrails
Serves the built UI and proxies API calls
Source, domain, table, row and PII scope
Controls stage transitions, bounded retries, model-call budgets and review pauses
Failed generated SQL: bounded schema / generation retry
User SQL edits return to validation
User reviews SQL and access scope
Arrows show request-stage order. Each agent stage returns control to the orchestrator.
Human control stays in the request flow
Approval pauses release workflow workers; models cannot approve SQL.
Clarification, refusal, cancellation or limits return a status to the user.
Visualization uses authorized results and does not execute new SQL.
Built-in JSON + published, versioned domain definitions
Concepts, metrics, rules, relationships and SQL examples
Lexical / BM25 retrieval; current-access mapping checks
LangChain typed tool calls and local handoff validation
Provider policy checks; credentials stay server-side
SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle
Mapped SQL Server joins across one server instance
Protected reads, PII/row scope and configured TLS
SQLite accounts, sessions, query and knowledge records
History retention, feedback and safe review checkpoints
Stage latency, provider usage and execution metrics
Drafts never enter generation context. Published knowledge supports intent, schema selection, column pruning, SQL and explanation.
Publishing, retirement or rollback invalidates old query approvals. Metadata validation does not prove business-result correctness.
Security is enforced by application code and database grants. Models cannot approve SQL or change data permissions.
